# Anne Shirley

## Overview

- **Age:** eleven years old  <sub>[v1 c6 P17](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0017)</sub>
- **Gender:** female  <sub>[v1 c6 P17](../source/v01-c06.md#nw-v01-c06-p0017)</sub>
- **Status:** alive  <sub>[v4 c1 P2](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0002)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v3 c3 P0](../source/v03-c03.md#nw-v03-c03-p0000)</sub>
- **Role:** country schoolma'am  <sub>[v3 c31 P1](../source/v03-c31.md#nw-v03-c31-p0001)</sub>

## Appearance

Anne is a girl with a little pointed chin, a nice nose, gray eyes, and bright red hair that she once accidentally dyed green before cutting it short. As a young child, her unbraided hair streamed behind her in a torrent of brightness. As she grew older, her bright hair and expressive face remained distinct features admired by her close friends.

_Sources: [v1 c13 P1](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0001), [v1 c15 P13](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0013), [v1 c15 P32](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0032), [v1 c27 P16](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0016), [v1 c27 P40](../source/v01-c27.md#nw-v01-c27-p0040), [v3 c4 P56](../source/v03-c04.md#nw-v03-c04-p0056), [v3 c22 P5](../source/v03-c22.md#nw-v03-c22-p0005)_

## Personality

Anne is an imaginative, enthusiastic, and talkative girl who throws herself into her studies and endeavors heart and soul. She possesses a vivid imagination that allows her to dream up elaborate scenarios, though it occasionally gets her into trouble or causes her to borrow unnecessary care. Intense in both her affections and her rivalries, she can hold grudges with strong tenacity, yet she is generous, courageous, and quick to take responsibility and confess when she realizes her mistakes.

_Sources: [v1 c12 P46](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0046), [v1 c13 P0](../source/v01-c13.md#nw-v01-c13-p0000), [v1 c15 P98](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0098), [v1 c17 P36](../source/v01-c17.md#nw-v01-c17-p0036), [v1 c19 P74](../source/v01-c19.md#nw-v01-c19-p0074), [v1 c20 P25](../source/v01-c20.md#nw-v01-c20-p0025), [v1 c24 P10](../source/v01-c24.md#nw-v01-c24-p0010), [v2 c2 P33](../source/v02-c02.md#nw-v02-c02-p0033)_

## History

Anne Shirley came to Green Gables as an eleven-year-old orphan and was taken in by Marilla and Matthew Cuthbert. She quickly formed a deep bond with her bosom friend Diana Barry and attended school in Avonlea under Mr. Phillips and later Miss Stacy. Driven by a intense academic rivalry with Gilbert Blythe, she excelled in her studies, joined the Queen's class, and earned her teacher's license at Queen's Academy. Although awarded the Avery scholarship, she gave up college to stay at home with Marilla after Matthew's death and taught at Avonlea school. During her time as a teacher, she served as secretary of the Avonlea Village Improvement Society and gained a neighborly friend in Mr. Harrison. She later attended Redmond College in Kingsport, rooming at Patty's Place with friends including Priscilla Grant and Philippa Gordon, before returning to teach as a country schoolma'am at Valley Road.

## Quotes

> Anne Shirley,” reluctantly faltered forth the owner of that name, “but, oh, please do call me Cordelia. It can’t matter much to you what you call me if I’m only going to be here a little while, can it? And Anne is such an unromantic name.  <sub>[v1 c3 P19](../source/v01-c03.md#nw-v01-c03-p0019)</sub>

> I shall never forgive Gilbert Blythe,” said Anne firmly. “And Mr. Phillips spelled my name without an e, too. The iron has entered into my soul, Diana.  <sub>[v1 c15 P51](../source/v01-c15.md#nw-v01-c15-p0051)</sub>

> I shall take more interest than ever in my studies now,” said Anne blissfully, “because I have a purpose in life. Mr. Allan says everybody should have a purpose in life and pursue it faithfully. Only he says we must first make sure that it is a worthy purpose. I would call it a worthy purpose to want to be a teacher like Miss Stacy, wouldn’t you, Marilla? I think it’s a very noble profession.  <sub>[v1 c30 P19](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0019)</sub>

> You both have the advantage of me,” sighed Anne. “You’re going to teach children who don’t know you, but I have to teach my own old schoolmates, and Mrs. Lynde says she’s afraid they won’t respect me as they would a stranger unless I’m very cross from the first. But I don’t believe a teacher should be cross. Oh, it seems to me such a responsibility!  <sub>[v2 c4 P1](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0001)</sub>

> Phil, you’re incorrigible. Well, I love you so much that I can’t make nice, light, congratulatory little speeches. But I’m heart-glad of your happiness.  <sub>[v3 c27 P32](../source/v03-c27.md#nw-v03-c27-p0032)</sub>
